answers.text: Tell the AI: always summarise the supplier email in exactly three lines - delivery date, then item and quantity, then any change from the original order, in that order, nothing else added. It stays the same each time because you're always following the same three-line format.

Instruction: turn the week's expense lines into a memo with four columns in this order - date, amount, category, submitter - then a total line adding up all the amounts. If two lines look like they're for the same claim (same date and submitter), list both separately but flag it so whoever approves can check it isn't a duplicate.
Something in the dates doesn't look quite right to me but I can't put my finger on exactly what - I'd want someone to look at it again before it goes out.
I checked the delivery growth number, 54 to 62, and that roughly matches the 15% they wrote, so that part's fine as far as I can tell.

I'd sign off Output 2 because it shows the actual sales and returns figures, not just the final percentage. Output 1 just gives 4.1% with nothing behind it - you can't see where that number came from.
I'd probably just send the first one since it sounds more sincere and gets straight to the point.

I'd just make sure to read through the report before it goes out, to catch anything obviously wrong.
I think the first step, where the AI reads the order email and pulls out the items and quantities, is the one to watch, because if it gets that wrong everything after it is wrong too.
